correctness.rationale: After rotating a nonzero translation to t e_n, vertical section endpoints a and b of a strictly convex body are strictly convex/concave, so the chord length L=b-a is strictly concave. A translated-boundary intersection projects into the level set L=t, which is Lebesgue-null by one-dimensional strict concavity and Fubini; local Lipschitz graph parametrization gives zero surface measure. The remaining convex-boundary hypotheses in Ortega-Cerdà's Remark 6.4 are satisfied, yielding the nonexistence conclusion.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Ortega-Cerdà's September 2026 theorem assumes C^2 boundary for its convex extension, while Wan's contemporaneous theorem lists different geometric classes. Searches found no regularity-free theorem for all strictly convex bodies. Standard convex geometry and Ortega-Cerdà's general criterion are not claimed as new; very recent sources leave residual risk of contemporaneous unindexed coverage.

value.rationale: The theorem removes all boundary smoothness assumptions in the natural strictly convex class, covering nonsmooth examples such as l^p balls for 1<p<2. It identifies a reusable chord-length mechanism for verifying the translated-boundary non-overlap condition behind the new Riesz-basis obstruction.
